articles.title_orig: Jimmy Kimmel Shames Trump for Suggesting Iran Could Bomb California
articles.title_zh: Jimmy Kimmel Shames Trump for Suggesting Iran Could Bomb California
articles.content_orig:
Donald Trump's remark that Iran could "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego has sparked fierce backlash from California politicians - and a strongly worded rebuttal from the White House.
California Governor Gavin Newsom condemned the comment - made by Trump at a campaign rally in Nebraska - as  "deranged and dangerous," while LA Mayor Karen Bass described them as threats and an attempt to "encourage attacks on American lives".
According to the White House, however, Trump was saying that American cities would have been threatened by Iran had he not launched a war there earlier this year.
Both LA and San Diego house major US military installations including Navy ports and Air Force bases.
Trump, while speaking on Monday in Nebraska about the Iran conflict, said: "It's a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, keeping our country safe. They can take out a city. Let them take out Los Angeles, let them take out San Diego."
There were cheers from sections of the audience as the comments about the two Californian cities were made.
The morning after Trump's statement, Governor Newsom announced that the "dangerous - if not treasonous" statement had prompted him to direct California's State Threat Assessment Center to "monitor the situation in the event that foreign actors interpret the remarks as an invitation" to target California.
The agency is designed to detect and prevent security threats in the state.
San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria wrote that the city was not collateral damage in a post on X, while demanding Trump keep it out of his "reckless war talk".
Trump is yet to respond to the statements made by California's leaders.
In a post on X, White House Communications Director Stephen Cheung described the "media freakout" over Trump's comments as "not rooted in reality".
"He was clearly stating US cities would have been threatened if a nuclear Iran hadn't been stopped," Cheung wrote. "America is safer because of the President. Iran has no nuclear, no navy, no air force, and no money".
The president and other administration officials often claim that disrupting Iran's nuclear programme was essential for US national security, and that any issues that have stemmed from the conflict were necessary.
A separate X post, from the official White House rapid response account, described journalists from the Los Angeles Times reporting on the comments as "buffoons" and again pushed back on the characterisation of the comments by Newsom and others.
"He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance," the account added.
San Diego, located 17 miles (27km) from the border with Mexico, is the eighth largest city in the US and is home to Naval Base San Diego, the home port of the US Navy's Pacific Fleet, and Naval Amphibious Base Coronado - the main training centre Navy Seals on the West Coast.
It is also where Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton is located, a base which 70,000 service members and civilians work at.
Located approximately 120 miles (193 KM) north of San Diego, Los Angeles is the second most populous city in the US.
It is home to the space system command headquarters of the US Space Force, as well as the Los Angeles Air Force Base.
This not the first time the US president and California governor, who may run for president in 2028, have publicly clashed.
Last year Trump described him as incompetent, saying he had failed to adequately respond after some of the Los Angeles anti-immigration enforcement protests turned violent.
Newsom accused Trump of a "brazen abuse of power" after military personnel were deployed to secure federal buildings during those protests.
Earlier this year, Trump mocked Newsom's dyslexia, saying presidents should not have learning disabilities, which led to criticism from dyslexia charities.

On 19 September 2026, the ReSea Women Influencers, Gizela Lucilia and Onésia Mazelete, joined the ReSea team and community focal points in a clean-up campaign across Vilankulo, Mozambique bringing together community groups, local institutions, civil society organisations and students in a shared commitment to a cleaner environment.

The initiative focused on the Vilankulo Municipal Market and other locations within the municipality, combining practical cleanup activities with environmental awareness on responsible waste management, cleaner public spaces and the importance of community participation in reducing pollution.
This collective effort brought together representatives from the Municipality of Vilankulo, the Associação Juvenil Para o Desenvolvimento Comunitário (AJUPADEC), the Youth Action for Climate Action Mozambique (YACAC-Moz), the Higher School of Rural Development (ESUDER), ParCo, and pupils from local primary and secondary schools. The ReSea team was represented by Gizela Lucilia, Onésia Mazelete, Anselmo Nhanenge and Elcídio Cossa, alongside community focal points Ivanilde and Joalina.
For the ReSea Women Influencers, participation in World Cleanup Day is an important part of their commitment to environmental stewardship and community engagement. Through initiatives such as this, they continue to strengthen their role in environmental awareness, community mobilisation and the protection of coastal communities.
Activities such as World Cleanup Day also reinforce the broader objectives of ReSea, particularly community engagement, environmental stewardship and the protection of coastal communities and ecosystems from pollution.
Cleaner and more resilient communities depend on sustained local action. In Vilankulo, this means bringing communities, institutions and young people together to take shared responsibility for the spaces and ecosystems on which they depend.
The Regenerative Seascapes for People, Climate and Nature (ReSea) Project is a multi-million dollar initiative funded by Global Affairs Canada under the Partnering for Climate engagement. articles.title_orig: Rising Stars: How VML Health’s Molly Kanofsky turns ‘an idea on a page’ into real-world impact
articles.title_zh: Rising Stars: How VML Health’s Molly Kanofsky turns ‘an idea on a page’ into real-world impact
articles.content_orig:
Molly Kanofsky had it all planned out. After years of picking up medical experience and focusing on the clinical side of the healthcare industry, she was going to go to back to school to become a physician assistant (PA) after graduating from the University of Delaware with her Bachelor of Applied Science. But instead of what was once her chosen path as a physician assistant, Kanofsky now finds herself in the pharma marketing world with VML Health after an unexpected career detour.
The door that closed on PA school opened to a new best-of-both-worlds career that merges her passion for healthcare and her creative abilities. After almost two years with BGB Group and another two with Havas Health Network in New York, Kanofsky started with VML Health in August as an account supervisor.
In a Q&A for Fierce Pharma Marketing’s “Rising Stars” series , Kanofsky explains her early career pivot, the excitement of learning as you go on a new project and the importance of leading with empathy and compassion.
Responses have been edited for length and clarity.
FPMK : What inspired you to pursue a career in pharma marketing, and what keeps you motivated in your current role?
I took a very unconventional route into pharma marketing. Even in high school, in college, I spent so much of my time pursuing the career of a PA, physician assistant. So I was volunteering in hospitals. I was working as a medical assistant, gaining as much clinical experience as I can, and then, unfortunately, I applied to PA school and I didn't get in. I was absolutely devastated. I feel like I was so tunnel visioned on that one goal that it was just really upsetting for me. I felt like I had failed, and I had no idea what I was supposed to do next because I really hadn't thought of any other career paths for me.
But I kind of realized that I wanted to go into healthcare because of impacting people's lives and just doing something that helps other people, so I just really needed to figure out another way to do it, and quite quickly because I'd graduated college and obviously needed an income of sorts. So my cousin actually worked for BGB Group for years, and he loved it. I heard about pharma marketing through him, and then I kind of researched what that would look like. And once I got in it, I realized I was able to combine my love for healthcare and then also my creative side, and it honestly just all clicked. And I realized, wow, this is a great field for me.
What keeps me motivated? I feel like there's two big things for me. More than anything is the people I work with. I've been really lucky to work on teams where everyone brings something different to the table, and I've learned so much from the people around me, so that is incredible. And then, second, I also love seeing something go from an idea on a page or just a simple conversation with your client or your team, and then that's actually put out into the real world. There's something very incredibly rewarding about being involved from the very beginning, working through all the challenges along the way with your team, and then finally seeing the end result make an impact on so many lives.
FPMK: What has been the most rewarding or challenging project that you've worked on so far?
So for the first couple years of my career, I was really in more of the traditional HCP marketing side of things. Then I had the opportunity in my last job to work on an account that was focused on partnering with physician influencers in the narcolepsy space to create content on a variety of social platforms, which is truly something I never heard of, like never heard before. It was still HCP to HCP education, but through a channel and format that was completely new to me and pretty new to my client as well. So because it was new for my client, we were really building a lot of the processes as we went, we worked in lockstep, figuring out what that should look like, what worked and what didn't, and how to bring the ideas to life within all the parameters we needed to work within.
I found myself getting more hands-on experience than I ever expected. There were moments where we needed a social mock-up to help visualize an idea, and I'd find myself in Canva putting together something. It was really everyone learning and figuring things out as we went. So there was very much a mentality of whatever needs to get done, we will figure out a way to do so, even if it wasn't like a typical process or like your standard timeline to get things done. We were like, 'we're gonna do whatever it takes to get this done, and we will figure it out.' So it was definitely one of the most challenging projects I've worked on because there were so many firsts, but that's also why it made it so rewarding as well.
FPMK: What advice would you give to people who worked in pharma marketing for decades?
I think the best thing someone with decades of experience can do is continue to share that experience generously while staying open to the people around them. I've been incredibly lucky to work with people who are much smarter and more experienced than I am, and I love that being around them makes me better.
I learn so much from how they think, how they approach challenges, and the perspective that they bring, but I also think the strongest teams recognize that everyone has something to contribute, regardless of how long they've been in the industry. And to me, that comes back to leading with empathy and compassion. When people feel supported, respected, and comfortable bringing their perspectives to the table, everyone learns from each other, and ultimately the work is better for it.
FPMK: What do you like to do when you're not working?
I live in New York, so my most favorite thing to do is really just walking everywhere, exploring different neighborhoods, and trying new restaurants. There's so many things, so many restaurants opening all the time. So it's so fun just going somewhere and trying something new. I spend as much time as possible with my boyfriend, my friends, my family, and I love traveling. I'm pretty much always planning my next trip. I'm actually going to Italy at the end of this week, so I'm so excited!

articles.title_orig: Russian Plague Scare: WHO Seeks Details About Reported Second Illness As Trump Plans Putin Call
articles.title_zh: Russian Plague Scare: WHO Seeks Details About Reported Second Illness As Trump Plans Putin Call
articles.content_orig:
A 28-year-old lab researcher at a Russian institute dedicated to studying plague and dangerous pathogens died of pneumonia of an “unknown” origin.
The Irkutsk Research Anti-Plague Institute operates in Siberia, where several other people are quarantined. Rospotrebnadzor, the Russian agency that oversees infectious disease, has downplayed the link between the researcher’s death and her work, but the case has prompted questions about the type of plague that causes pneumonia.
The US State Department and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said they are monitoring the situation closely. The World Health Organization said Monday it’s in contact with Russian health authorities to verify what happened, what testing is underway and any potential international public health implications.
Dozens quarantined after researcher at Russian plague laboratory dies of ‘unknown’ infection
“Based on unofficial information available, the public health risk to the general population appears to be low,” a WHO spokesperson said, adding that its risk assessment would be updated once more information was available.
Pneumonic plague is a rare, deadly lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Scientists consider pneumonic plague the most dangerous form of the infection.
There are other forms of plague stemming from Y. pestis that attack different parts of the body.
The most common form, bubonic plague, often develops after a flea bite or when the bacterium enters through a cut or break in the skin. The infection triggers swollen, painful lymph nodes and can progress to septicemic plague.
Septicemic plague infects the bloodstream, potentially leading to organ failure, it can also come directly from a flea bite.
Pharyngeal plague attacks the throat after someone eats infected meat.
Pneumonic plague is the only form of the bacterial infection that passes directly from person to person. Respiratory particles carry it when a person coughs or sneezes. Droplets from infected animals can also transmit it.
The last documented person-to-person transmission of pneumonic plague in the United States dates back to 1924, during an outbreak in Los Angeles .
With pneumonic plague, particles lodge in the lungs and can trigger severe pneumonia, making breathing difficult. Symptoms can begin within 24 hours of infection.
Other symptoms include fever, chills, headache, body aches, dizziness, weakness, fatigue, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
Without treatment, it is nearly always deadly.
Doctors can treat plague with at least 10 to 14 days of antibiotics. Most commonly they use ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, gentamicin, and streptomycin. Patients that get antibiotics within the first 24 hours of infection have the best chance of surviving.
Doctors may also support someone with supportive care and provide supplemental oxygen, fluids and encouragement to rest.
Although plague vaccines have been in use since the 19th century, it wasn’t clear they offer protection from pneumonic plague.
The WHO doesn’t recommend vaccination , except for high-risk groups such as laboratory personnel who are constantly exposed to the risk of contamination.
Although people may be most familiar with plague from reading the Bible or historical literature — or as a metaphor to describe broader pestilence and poverty, according to infectious disease expert Dr. Tyler Evans — it persists today.
Known as the “Black Death” in the 14th century, the infection killed more than 50 million people in Europe. While antibiotics have made it more manageable, it remains present on every continent except Oceania.
Since the 1990s, most human cases have occurred in Africa, according to the WHO.
The last US death from pneumonic plague occurred in Arizona in July 2025, according to the CDC . The young man worked with sick cats and is believed to have contracted the infection from the animals. No one else exposed to the cats reported getting sick.
Evans, who wrote “ Pandemics, Poverty and Politics: Decoding the Social and Political Drivers of Pandemics from Plague to Covid-19 ,” says the risk for plague is “getting worse as the result of ecological changes and particularly with the US pulling back on our public health infrastructure and measures.”
Plague, at least, can be quick to diagnose, he said. And “the antibiotics, first and second line, are very effective for this.”
WHO has said the risk to the general population appears to be low.
People with pneumonic plague feel sick very quickly, which can slow potential spread, according to Dr. Rutul Dalal, an infectious disease physician at Penn State Health St. Joseph Medical Center.
“It’s very difficult for someone to even walk, do their daily activities, let alone travel,” Dalal said. People can develop symptoms as early as 24 hours after exposure.
There are no direct flights between Russia and the US, he said, so by the time an infected person would reach the US they would likely already be exhibiting symptoms.
“Of course, you have to be careful, and you should keep this at the back of your mind … The world is a little village now, as I say — connected to each other. But at this point in time, compared to what we have been seeing, like during the Covid pandemic, this is not of that magnitude as of now, and hopefully remains contained as it is.”
For people around patients with plague, WHO recommends avoiding direct contact with those who are sick and urges caution around infected body fluids.
Workers caring for patients with pneumonic plague must wear standard protective equipment and may also take preventive antibiotics.
In case of exposure, health officials will also monitor family members and other close contacts of an infected person and provide them with antibiotics before they become ill. They also recommend routine hand-washing with soap and water.

articles.title_orig: Alpha Cognition to Present New ZUNVEYL® (Benzgalantamine) Clinical and Real-World Data at ASCP Annual Meeting and NEI Fall Congress
articles.title_zh: Alpha Cognition to Present New ZUNVEYL® (Benzgalantamine) Clinical and Real-World Data at ASCP Annual Meeting and NEI Fall Congress
articles.content_orig:
Presentations will highlight data on cognition, function, neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep, gastrointestinal tolerability, treatment patterns and psychotropic medication utilization in Alzheimer’s disease
VANCOUVER, British Columbia & DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Alpha Cognition Inc. (Nasdaq: ACOG) (“Alpha Cognition” or the “Company”), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, today announced that new clinical and real-world data on ZUNVEYL and acetylcholinesterase inhibitors will be presented at the American Society of Consultant Pharmacists (ASCP) Annual Meeting, taking place October 29-November 1, 2026 and Neuroscience Education Institute (NEI) Fall Congress, taking place November 5-8, 2026.
The presentations span multiple aspects of Alzheimer’s disease care and ZUNVEYL use, including cognition, activities of daily living, neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep, gastrointestinal tolerability, treatment patterns and psychotropic medication utilization. Together, the analyses provide additional insights into the use of ZUNVEYL and acetylcholinesterase inhibitors in long-term care and other real-world settings.
The Company will present the following posters:
“The breadth of data being presented at ASCP and NEI Fall Congress reflects our continued commitment to building the scientific evidence around ZUNVEYL,” said Dr. Denis Kay, Chief Scientific Officer of Alpha Cognition. “These analyses examine multiple aspects of treatment in Alzheimer’s disease, including cognition, function, neuropsychiatric symptoms, sleep, tolerability and medication utilization, and provide additional real-world insights that can help inform our understanding of ZUNVEYL use in clinical practice.”
About Alpha Cognition Inc.
Alpha Cognition Inc. is a commercial stage, biopharmaceutical company dedicated to developing treatments for patients with neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease and Cognitive Impairment with mild Traumatic Brain Injury (“mTBI”), for which there are currently no approved treatment options.
ZUNVEYL is a patented drug approved as a new generation acetylcholinesterase inhibitor for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease, with expected minimal gastrointestinal side effects. ZUNVEYL’s active metabolite is differentiated from donepezil and rivastigmine in that it binds neuronal nicotinic receptors, most notably the alpha-7 subtype, which is known to have a positive effect on cognition. ALPHA-1062 is also being developed in combination with memantine to treat moderate to severe Alzheimer’s dementia, and as an intranasal formulation for Cognitive Impairment with mTBI.
ZUNVEYL is a cholinesterase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of mild to moderate dementia of the Alzheimer’s type in adults.
IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION
ZUNVEYL is contraindicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to benzgalantamine, galantamine, or to any inactive ingredients in ZUNVEYL. Serious skin reactions have occurred.
Serious Skin Reactions : Serious skin reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome and acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis) have been reported in patients receiving galantamine (the active metabolite of ZUNVEYL tablets). If signs or symptoms suggest a serious skin reaction, use of this drug should not be resumed, and alternative therapy should be considered.
Anesthesia : See Drug Interactions Section
Cardiovascular Conditions: Cholinesterase inhibitors, including ZUNVEYL, have vagotonic effects on the sinoatrial and atrioventricular nodes, leading to bradycardia and AV block. Bradycardia and all types of heart block have been reported in patients taking cholinesterase inhibitors, both with and without known underlying cardiac conduction abnormalities. Therefore, all patients should be considered at risk for adverse effects on cardiac conduction.
Patients treated with galantamine up to 24 mg/day using the recommended dosing schedule showed a dose-related increase in risk of syncope.
Gastrointestinal Conditions : Cholinesterase inhibitors, including ZUNVEYL, may increase gastric acid secretion. Patients should be monitored closely for active or occult gastrointestinal bleeding, especially those with a history of ulcer disease or those receiving concurrent nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs). Clinical studies of galantamine have shown no increase, relative to placebo, in the incidence of either peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding.
Galantamine has been shown to produce nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, anorexia, and weight loss . Monitor the patient’s weight during therapy with ZUNVEYL.
Genitourinary Conditions: Although this was not observed in clinical trials with galantamine, cholinesterase inhibitors, including ZUNVEYL, may cause bladder outflow obstruction.
Neurological Conditions: Cholinesterase inhibitors are believed to have some potential to cause generalized convulsions. Seizure activity may also be a manifestation of Alzheimer’s disease. Patients with Alzheimer’s disease should be monitored closely for seizures while taking ZUNVEYL.
Pulmonary Conditions: Cholinesterase inhibitors, including ZUNVEYL, should be prescribed with care to patients with a history of severe asthma or obstructive pulmonary disease. Monitor for respiratory adverse reactions.
The most common adverse reactions with galantamine tablets (≥5%) were nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, and decreased appetite.
Use with Anticholinergics: Galantamine has the potential to interfere with the activity of anticholinergic medications.
Use with Cholinomimetics and Other Cholinesterase Inhibitors: A synergistic effect is expected when cholinesterase inhibitors are given concurrently with succinylcholine, other cholinesterase inhibitors, similar neuromuscular blocking agents or cholinergic agonists such as bethanechol.
USE IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS
Pregnancy: Based on animal data may cause fetal harm.
Hepatic Impairment: In patients with moderate hepatic impairment, a decrease in clearance of galantamine was observed; therefore, a dosage adjustment is recommended. Use of ZUNVEYL in patients with severe hepatic impairment is not recommended.
Renal Impairment: In patients with a creatinine clearance of 9 to 59 mL/min, an increase in exposure of galantamine was observed; therefore, a dosage adjustment is recommended. Use of ZUNVEYL in patients with creatinine clearance less than 9 mL/min is not recommended.
These are not all of the possible side effects of ZUNVEYL. You can report side effects to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/MedWatch or call 1‑800‑FDA‑1088. Please click here for Full Prescribing Information .
Forward-looking Statements
This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of applicable securities laws. Forward-looking statements include, without limitation, statements regarding the presentation, interpretation, significance and potential impact of clinical and real-world data relating to ZUNVEYL® (benzgalantamine), the potential benefits and profile of ZUNVEYL, the Company's commercialization activities, and the future development of its product candidates.
Forward-looking statements are based on management's current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by such statements. articles.title_orig: Stock futures little changed after S&P 500 hits fresh record: Live updates
articles.title_zh: Stock futures little changed after S&P 500 hits fresh record: Live updates
articles.content_orig:
U.S. equity futures inched lower early Wednesday after the S&P 500 reached a fresh all-time intraday high and a record close in the previous session, driven by a tech stock rally.
Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 0.09%, while S&P 500 futures were flat and Nasdaq-100 futures were down 0.21%.
In trading on Tuesday, the S&P 500 gained 0.58%, marking its fourth positive session in a row and closing above a level of 7,800 for the first time. The Dow gained 0.49%, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.45%.
Chipmakers were the big winners on Tuesday, with Marvell Technology gaining 5.8% on higher revenue guidance and Advanced Micro Devices climbing 2.8% after Citi hiked its price target, citing rising demand for central processing units.
Bond yields took a break on Tuesday from the steady march upward they began at the end of February, coinciding with the start of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. Treasury yields moved higher on Wednesday ahead of a closely watched 10-year note auction .
Investors warned Tuesday about falling foreign demand for U.S. debt amid geopolitical pressures.
"The Chinese don't want to continue to accumulate," investor Ray Dalio told Bloomberg. "When you have a debtor-creditor relationship and you have an adversary relationship, that's a very difficult dynamic."
Investors are awaiting the minutes of the Federal Reserve's last meeting in September, at which the U.S. central bank raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. Minutes are set to shed light on how monetary policymakers are thinking about economic conditions.
In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 0.92% lower as the broader Topix fell 0.7%. South Korea's Kospi declined nearly 2%, while the small-cap Kosdaq lost 2.34%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 ended flat. The mainland China market remained closed for the Golden Week holiday.
Shares listed in Europe opened broadly lower on Wednesday, with the regional Stoxx 600 index down 0.4% shortly after the bell.
The chief executive of U.S. oil giant Chevron on Wednesday warned it would be "unwise" for the Trump administration to move forward with a diesel export ban , saying the policy runs the risk of making the supply situation worse.
"The U.S. has been a reliable supplier to the world at a time when it needs it," Chevron CEO Mike Wirth told CNBC's " Squawk Box Europe " in an exclusive interview on Wednesday.
"And I think it would be unwise for the U.S. to create questions in the minds of our allies and our partners as to whether or not we will be there with reliable supply when times are difficult — and so, there are other options," he added.
Average house prices in the U.K. were flat in September, according to data from lender Lloyds , after falling 0.3% the previous month.
The average property price in the country is now £298,441 ($395,005), compared to £298,395 in August. The index was also flat on an annual basis.
"While the market overall has been fairly subdued, property prices have so far proved resilient during a period of higher mortgage rates, which has been driven by changing expectations around the future path of Base Rate," Andrew Asaam, mortgages director at Lloyds, said in the data release. "That's mirrored in wider economic data, with household spending holding up better than many expected despite energy and other cost pressures arising from the Middle East conflict."
Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 0.92% lower at 70,035.71, and the broader Topix fell 0.70% to 4,154.11.
South Korea's Kospi declined nearly 2% to 6,803.90, while the small-cap Kosdaq lost 2.34% to 898.43.
Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 ended flat at 8,727.70.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index was down 0.50% as of its last hour of trade on Wednesday. Mainland China market remained closed for the Golden Week holiday.
Shares listed in Europe opened broadly lower on Wednesday, with the regional Stoxx 600 index down 0.4% shortly after the bell.
Mining and tech stocks led losses, while Germany's DAX — down 0.9% — notched the biggest decline among major regional bourses.
Yields on bonds issued by various governments moved higher on Wednesday morning, amid lingering economic concerns.
The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury was up 4 basis points to 5.309% as of 2:30 a.m. ET. Yields on the longer-maturity 30-year Treasury note added almost 5 basis points to 5.688%.
Bond yields and prices move in opposite directions.
Yields on U.K. government bonds, known as gilts, also rose across the curve, with 10- and 20-year bond yields rising by 5 basis points.
Meanwhile, French and Italian 10-year government bond yields rose by 8 basis points. Japanese bonds bucked the trend, with yields trading marginally lower.
NLFI, a non-profit organization that manages shares of nationalized or bailed-out financial institutions owned by the Dutch state, said Wednesday that it would sell part of its stake in lender ABN Amro.
The sale would be carried out through a pre-arranged trading plan, executed by BofA Securities Europe, it said. Once completed, it would reduce NLFI's holding of ABN Amro to a 10.5% stake, down from 20.7%.
The Reserve Bank of India on Wednesday raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, joining several major central banks in tightening monetary policy to arrest accelerating inflation.
The central bank increased the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to a 1-year high of 5.50%, in line with expectations of economists polled by Reuters.
India's economic growth has been strong despite global challenges, Sanjay Malhotra, RBI governor, said in his address on Wednesday, while adding that "inflation and its outlook are not benign, as they were last year."
The monetary policy committee decided to change the policy stance "to calibrated tightening," Malhotra said.
The hike comes as retail inflation in India has been on the rise for 10 straight months , touching 4.8% in August, higher than the RBI's medium-term target of 4%.
Oil rose Wednesday as attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia raised concerns over crude flows from the Middle East even as supplies have been recovering.
Futures for international benchmark Brent crude for December delivery gained 1.17% at $101.76 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for November advanced 1.26% at $90.57 per barrel.
Naeem Aslam, chief investment officer of Zaye Capital Markets, said Tuesday that oil remains "caught between improving physical supply and persistent geopolitical risk."
"The sustained ability of the Houthis in Yemen to target oil facilities hundreds of kilometers from the border keeps the risks of a renewed large-scale crude supply disruption present and high, and these risks could worsen if the Houthis feel the need to apply more pressure as a result of losing more territory," said Samer Hasn, senior market analyst at forex trading platform XS.com.
Hong Kong shares fell Wednesday, amid broad declines in other Asian markets as oil prices rose.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell 0.65%, with declines led by healthcare and tech sectors, down 1.32% and 0.63%, respectively.
Mainland China market remained closed for the Golden Week holiday.
Asian stocks opened mixed on Wednesday.
Japan's Nikkei 225 was flat at the open, while the Topix added 0.18%. South Korea's Kospi was down 0.57% and the small-cap Kosdaq was down 0.27%.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 lost 0.13%.
Mainland China markets remain closed for a holiday.
Asian stocks were poised to open mixed on Wednesday, diverging from gains on Wall Street where the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed at fresh records.
Japan's Nikkei 225 was set to rise at open, with its Chicago and Osaka futures contracts last at 71,020 and 70,070 respectively, compared with the index's previous close of 70,683.98.
Futures for Hong Kong's Hang Seng index stood at 24,272, marginally lower than its last close of 24,280.56.
Futures for Australia's S&P/ASX 200 were at 8,771, while the index closed at 8735.7
Mainland China markets remain closed

articles.title_orig: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Bertelsmann is the World’s Biggest Book Publisher
articles.title_zh: Frankfurt Book Fair 2026: Bertelsmann is the World’s Biggest Book Publisher
articles.content_orig:
The title of the world’s largest book publisher has changed hands once again, according to data compiled by consultant Rüdiger Wischenbart and the editors from Digital Publishing Report. In the recently released 2025 Global Publishing Ranking, Bertelsmann surpassed the 2024 leader, Thomson Reuters, which slipped to third place. Bertelsmann, the Germany-based owner of Penguin Random House, posted book publishing revenue of $6.98 billion last year, with $5.86 billion coming from PRH. Thomson Reuters’s book revenue rose from $6.24 billion to $6.62 billion, but that wasn’t enough to keep it atop the list.
In second place was RELX, with sales of $6.53 billion. Wolters Kluwer posted a 17% jump in sales to just over $5 billion, moving it into fourth place ahead of Pearson, whose sales increased 7.8% to $4.82 billion.
The scientific publisher Springer Nature (#7) had a solid 2025 with revenue topping $2 billion for the first time thanks to a 18% sales increase over 2024. Japan’s Hitotsubashi Group (#8) stayed in the top 10 thanks in large part to the success of manga publishers Shueisha and Shogakukan.
As noted by Wischenbart, the 10 largest publishers accounted for well over half of all revenue generated by the publishers on the list (56%, up from 55% in 2024). Publishers falling in the 11th to 20th spots accounted for another 20% of revenue.
According to Wischenbart’s analysis, STM and professional publishers accounted for 49% of all revenue of the publishers included in the ranking, while trade publishers generated 32% of sales and educational publishers 19%.
The largest U.S.-based publisher on the list is HarperCollins (#9), which had revenue of $2.15 billion in the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025. McGraw-Hill, another U.S. publisher, was in 10th place, with sales for the fiscal year ended Mar. 31, 2026, holding at $2.10 billion.
The latest ranking does not include Simon & Schuster, because the publisher has not disclosed its revenue since 2023, when it was acquired by the private equity firm KKR. The last reported figure was $1.04 billion, which would put S&S just outside the 20 largest publishers.
Jim Milliot is editor-at-large at Publishers Weekly .

articles.title_orig: U.S. News & World Report Partners with Candid to Bring Agentic AI Survey Innovation to Senior Living
articles.title_zh: U.S. News & World Report Partners with Candid to Bring Agentic AI Survey Innovation to Senior Living
articles.content_orig:
Strategic partnership modernizes how senior living operators capture real-time resident and family feedback.
WASHINGTON , Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- U.S. News & World Report, the global authority in healthcare decision support, today announced a strategic partnership with and investment in Candid, an AI-powered engagement start-up serving senior living and post-acute care organizations, to modernize feedback collection and advance resident engagement and quality measurement standards across the senior living industry.
Through the partnership, U.S. News and Candid equip senior living communities to move beyond traditional static questionnaires through AI-powered, conversational engagement tools. The integration expands the tools available to operators to capture real-time insights from residents and their families, turning direct resident and family input into measurable quality improvements.
This collaboration comes at a pivotal time for the senior care sector. With 10,000 Americans reaching retirement age daily – known as "The Peak 65 Phenomenon" – the need for transparent, reliable data to guide family care decisions and evaluate community performance continues to grow. Building on U.S. News' 2026 Best Senior Living ratings , which evaluated communities based on feedback from more than 540,000 consumer surveys, U.S. News continues to lead efforts to standardize resident engagement measures and bring modern, data-driven capabilities to senior living operators and care providers.
"For five years, U.S. News' Best Senior Living ratings have provided families with trusted data and benchmarks as they evaluate their senior living options," said Sumita Singh, executive vice president and general manager of Health at U.S. News. "As millions of older adults enter retirement, improving how senior living communities capture resident and family feedback is a must. Our strategic partnership with Candid reflects our commitment to bringing frictionless technologies to senior living operators so they can gather real-time resident and family feedback across all modalities."
Candid's platform uses interactive voice and text conversations that allow residents, family members and employees to provide feedback in their own words. The platform combines quantitative metrics with qualitative sentiment analysis, identifying recurring themes, emerging operational concerns and trends.
Across current deployments – which span hundreds of senior living communities nationwide – Candid's conversational format averages an approximate 70 percent response rate, drastically outperforming traditional survey channels.
"Senior living organizations have historically had to choose between collecting structured data at scale and having meaningful conversations with residents, families, and employees," said Raphael Rubens, founder and CEO of Candid. "AI allows us to combine both, understand what is driving the feedback and turn those insights into action, ultimately improving the experience and quality of care for residents."
About U.S. News & World Report U.S. News & World Report is the global leader for journalism that empowers consumers, citizens, business leaders and policy officials to make confident decisions in all aspects of their lives and communities. A multifaceted media company, U.S. News provides unbiased rankings, independent reporting and analysis, and consumer advice to millions of people on USNews.com each month. A pillar in Washington for more than 90 years, U.S. News is the trusted home for in-depth and exclusive insights on education, health, politics, the economy, insurance, personal finance, travel, automobiles, real estate, careers and consumer products and services.
About Candid Candid Technology, Inc. ("Candid") is an AI powered engagement platform for senior living and post acute care. Its technology helps organizations collect resident, family, and employee feedback, improve online reputation, understand retention, and automate frontline applicant engagement and interviews. Candid has been deployed across hundreds of communities throughout the United States and is backed by leading investors. For more information, visit callcandid.com .

articles.title_orig: France’s student protests highlight a debt crisis that could spill over to the rest of Europe
articles.title_zh: France’s student protests highlight a debt crisis that could spill over to the rest of Europe
articles.content_orig:
France’s unprecedented wave of student protests has laid bare the country’s growing financial pressures, which will only become more difficult to tackle as Europe’s second-largest economy tries to rein in a ballooning budget deficit.
The country’s finances are in a precarious state. Public debt was more than $4 trillion in June, exceeding the size of the economy, according to the country’s statistics agency . The cost of servicing that debt has climbed by billions of dollars on last year, as bond yields spike .
At the same time, demands on the public purse are rising: Pension costs have climbed because of an aging population while the government looks to spend more on defense.
High school students, meanwhile, have called for a fix to staff shortages, overcrowded classrooms and crumbling school infrastructure.
Solutions to France’s financial troubles have led to social unrest in the past. Efforts to raise the retirement age sparked widespread protests in 2023 .
French school protests grow as workers join students
Last week, the French government proposed deep spending cuts and tax hikes aimed at narrowing the budget deficit, but bond buyers are concerned that fiscal measures may be watered down by lawmakers ahead of presidential elections next year, said Andrew Kenningham, chief European economist at consultancy Capital Economics.
The election could see President Emmanuel Macron ousted by either a far-right or far-left successor, raising questions over the country’s commitment to fiscal discipline. While Marine Le Pen’s right-wing National Rally recently proposed substantial spending cuts meant to stabilize the public finances, her party also remains committed to costly tax reductions, Kenningham said.
“Investors will also be concerned about greater fiscal populism after the elections,” he wrote in a note last week. “There is a big risk that spreads rise a lot further, either before or after next year’s elections.”
Worries about a potential debt crisis in France boiled over last week, leading to a selloff in French bonds and a sharp rise in yields.
The spread between French and German bond yields expanded to its widest level since 2012. That difference in yields means investors are demanding much higher returns to hold debt from France compared with Germany, which is deemed a safer alternative.
The French bond rout has sparked fears of spillovers to other high-yield European debt markets, with some analysts drawing parallels with the eurozone debt crisis of the early 2010s .
Global bond sell-off deepens, sending borrowing costs higher around the world
Given France’s size and systemic importance, “the potential for contagion into other countries and the Eurozone at large is very large and could potentially cause a serious crisis for the entire region,” Angel Talavera, chief European economist at Oxford Economics, an advisory firm, told CNN.
These worries in large part pushed the euro to its weakest level against the dollar since May 2025 on Monday. The currency, shared by 21 countries in the European Union, is worth around $1.12, having briefly dipped below that level.
The latest ructions in markets could weigh on a fragile economic recovery in Europe, bolstered by investment into artificial intelligence, stronger demand for European exports and higher defense spending in Germany.
Recent survey data showed that activity in manufacturing and services in the euro area increased at its fastest pace in nearly three-and-a-half years last month.
“(Economic) growth is staging a comeback and Europe has shown surprising resilience,” economists at Morgan Stanley wrote in a late September note.
Fall of yet another premier will make it hard for France to fix its finances. What’s behind its debt problem?
High bond yields are a clear risk to that growth, however.
If governments don’t cut spending , “interest rates will continue to go up,” Carsten Brzeski, head of macroeconomics at Dutch bank ING told CNN.
Higher bond yields push up the cost of borrowing throughout the economy, making home and car purchases more expensive and driving down investment. They also make it more expensive for governments to borrow money and force a certain degree of austerity to stop yields from rising further.
Yields on French, German and UK government bonds have broken multi-year records in recent weeks as concerns mount about the sustainability of public debt loads.
Europe’s public finances pose “serious risks to eurozone financial markets and to the economy,” Jack Allen-Reynolds, deputy chief eurozone economist at Capital Economics, told CNN.

articles.title_orig: EU negotiators head to China hoping to curb cheap imports of hybrid electric cars
articles.title_zh: EU negotiators head to China hoping to curb cheap imports of hybrid electric cars
articles.content_orig:
Mood in trade talks said to have changed as EU member states harden demands for protection against Chinese imports
EU trade negotiators are heading to China for two days of crunch talks aimed at sealing a breakthrough deal tackling Beijing’s record £1bn-a-day trade surplus by curbing its exports of cheap hybrid electric cars into Europe .
Trade commissioner Maroš Šefčovič and his team fly out on Wednesday and will be negotiating up to the wire in talks scheduled to start the following day and continue late into Friday.
Sources say they hope to achieve “tangible, meaningful and measurable” results before the meeting of EU leaders in Brussels on Thursday next week, where China is high on the agenda.
The main focus is on what has been described as a “proof of concept” pilot agreement involving one sector, which is expected to be cars, which could be scaled up for other sectors in the coming months.
Diplomatic efforts to avert a full-scale trade war started at the end of June, albeit with little hope that China could curb exports to the EU given its historic ability to pivot quickly any time trade barriers are put in its path. For example, after the EU imposed tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles in October 2024 there was a boom in exports of hybrid cars , which were not subject to tariffs.
Last month, the EU asked China to voluntarily restrict hybrid exports to address soaring sales, warning that if they did not restrict them, safeguards – which could include quotas – could be enacted.
It is not known what China’s response was. But sources say the mood in talks has changed as EU member states have hardened demands for protection against Chinese imports that threaten their own industries.
On Monday, Germany’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz, agreed a “historic U-turn” on its policy on China by siding with the French president, Emmanuel Macron, in authorising effective permission for EU leaders to approve a new instrument to allow them to defend trade by cutting access to the single market at short notice.
In a joint paper with Emmanuel Macron, the two countries spoke of “a massive industrial shock … affecting sectors at the heart of the European industrial model and of systemic relevance [pharmaceuticals, aerospace, automotive, machine tools, chemicals, etc.]”.
The paper called for the use of all existing trade defence tools, but also for a new diversification instrument and “possible additional” new measures to allow the bloc to react when “third countries seek to undermine the restoration of a level playing field”.
Andrew Small, a former EU adviser on China, said Šefčovič’s talks will test the resolve of both Beijing and Brussels and will “determine whether China is willing to put sufficiently serious offers on the table”.
Small, who is the Asia director at the European Council on Foreign Relations in Berlin, warned: “China’s most effective tactic may be to draw Europe into a ‘process trap’ offering just enough to delay action, without addressing the forces driving European deindustrialisation.”
after newsletter promotion
Sources say the Franco-German proposals for a new instrument, dubbed a “kill switch”, were born out of frustration, particularly in Paris, that a so-called “trade bazooka” available to Brussels, officially known as the anti-coercion instrument, has never been used.
Paris pushed for the use of the ACI following Trump’s threat of tariffs last year but it never gained traction from others as it could take up to a year to implement.
Handlesblatt, the Germany business newspaper, described Monday’s change in policy as “nothing less than an economic turning point”, with chief political reporter Martin Greive concluding in a hard-hitting column that Merz was “putting an end to years of naiveté towards Beijing”.
“Merz has recognised in recent months that Germany is the epicentre of the China shock 2.0; that there might not be much left of German industry if Germany continues to stand by and watch as China gains enormous export advantages through trillions in subsidies, the unilateral siphoning off of knowhow, and a – to put it mildly – questionable monetary policy,” he wrote.

articles.title_orig: Isaias: Gulf Coast faces hurricane threat as Tropical Depression Nine is forecast to strengthen
articles.title_zh: Isaias: Gulf Coast faces hurricane threat as Tropical Depression Nine is forecast to strengthen
articles.content_orig:
[Breaking news update, published at 5 a.m. ET]
Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the southwestern Gulf on Wednesday morning, according to the National Hurricane Center. It’s forecast to become the first hurricane of the Atlantic season Thursday and strengthen into a Category 2 by Friday.
The storm has sustained winds of 40 mph and is located about 600 miles south of the mouth of the Mississippi River.
A strengthening tropical depression is primed to become Hurricane Isaias and batter parts of the southern US this week with heavy rain and strong winds.
Tropical Depression Nine has sustained winds of 35 mph and was located about 600 miles south of the mouth of the Mississippi River as of Tuesday evening.
Get live updates and alerts. Download the CNN Weather app.
The system is expected to push east above the Yucatan Peninsula and then turn sharply north toward the northern Gulf Coast. It’s forecast to strengthen quickly and become a Category 2 hurricane with 100 mph winds by Friday.
Isaias will likely usher in flooding rain, powerful winds and storm surge, to areas from southern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle beginning on Friday. The storm could also spin up several tornadoes as its rainbands lash the coast.
This will be the first hurricane of the year in the Atlantic basin, ending a record-long wait tied to the effects of a likely record-strong El Niño .
Exactly where the storm could track or how strong it will be when it approaches land are still not set in stone, but anyone along the Gulf Coast from Louisiana to Florida’s Big Bend should monitor the forecast closely.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis declared a state of emergency for 25 counties Tuesday ahead of the storm, urging residents to prepare disaster plans and stock hurricane supply kits. State emergency teams are staging generators, fuel, food, water and flood barriers in the Tallahassee and Santa Rosa areas to support the response.
Oil companies are also taking precautions in the Gulf. Shell is evacuating nonessential personnel from six offshore platforms, while BP is removing nonessential workers and securing its offshore facilities, the companies said Tuesday.
This storm is making a run through El Niño-influenced atmospheric conditions that have largely stymied tropical systems throughout the Atlantic hurricane season so far. Gulf waters are record warm for this time of year, providing plenty of fuel, but that’s only part of the equation.
The bane of Atlantic tropical systems this season has been wind shear. This refers to winds blowing at different speeds and from different directions at several levels of the atmosphere. Wind shear can tear tropical storms and hurricanes apart.
This new system is benefitting from low wind shear in the southern Gulf, but it’ll find higher wind shear guarding the Gulf Coast to the north, threatening to shred the storm as it makes its approach.
But the system is also forecast to move quickly, so its exposure to the higher wind shear may be limited. If the storm were to move slower, it could weaken quickly as it meanders in hostile conditions.
The storm’s strength and path are also intertwined. A stronger storm’s circulation extends higher into the atmosphere, allowing winds at those heights to steer it differently than a weaker system. That path, in turn, will determine how long it spends over warm water and how much hostile wind shear it encounters, shaping how strong it is when it reaches the coast.
No matter its final fate, heavy rain is a concern on the Gulf Coast and in other parts of the South by late this week. The storm could bring 3 to 6 inches of rain, with localized rainfall up to 10 inches in spots, from southern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle and Big Bend. The downpours could start to ramp up along the coast as soon as Friday and then continue to soak the region while creeping farther inland through the weekend.
As this year has already shown, it doesn’t take a hurricane-strength system to cause significant impacts, particularly in a warming world that’s making tropical systems wetter.
Tropical storms Arthur and Edouard didn’t last long, but their heavy rain resulted in significant flash flooding and water rescues. Parts of Louisiana and Mississippi took the brunt of Arthur’s flooding while Edouard dropped over 20 inches of rain in eastern Texas.
Pinning down the location and severity of any storm surge flooding, strong winds and tornadoes along the northern Gulf Coast is even more difficult this far out in time because we need to know how strong the storm will be and exactly where it will track. The earliest those impacts could arrive is late Friday or Saturday.
Four named storms — that’s tropical storm strength or greater — typically form in October and November, but some hurricane seasons can have a stronger finish while others quiet down.
The last few years illustrate this year-to-year ebb and flow. Seven storms formed during October and November in 2024, but just two formed during the same time in 2023.
Late-season storms tend to form closer to the United States, including in the Gulf, Caribbean and off the Southeast coast, which makes them more likely to impact land.
While there are usually fewer storms, they can still be destructive.
Last year, Category 5 Hurricane Melissa devastated Jamaica in October’s final week.
Hurricane Michael roared into the Florida Panhandle on October 10, 2018, becoming the latest landfalling Category 5 on record in the US. And Hurricane Sandy may be the most notorious of all: It morphed into a hybrid superstorm in late-October 2012 and walloped the East Coast.
Super El Niño’s grip on the Atlantic basin means a repeat of notorious late-season hurricanes is less likely this year. Its storm-killing wind is the main reason this season could go hurricane-free for the first time in reliable records .

articles.title_orig: Measles case confirmed in Allegheny County with possible exposure at Target, health dept. says
articles.title_zh: Measles case confirmed in Allegheny County with possible exposure at Target, health dept. says
articles.content_orig:
The Allegheny County Health Department said an unvaccinated minor under 18 years old has tested positive for measles and is recovering at home.
It's the first confirmed case of measles involving an Allegheny County resident this year, according to Monday's announcement by the health department.
The health department said people who visited the Target store at Pine Creek Shopping Center on McKnight Road between 3:45 p.m. and 5:45 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 1, may have been exposed. The store is located in McCandless.
"Not happy. But I feel confident I've gotten enough vaccines…” said Wexford resident Allison Arend, who said she was at the McCandless Target during the time of possible exposure. “I feel pretty confident, but not exactly happy that it happened at my own home Target.”
Health officials said no additional information about the patient will be released, citing privacy reasons, but they said there were no school-related exposures.
"Measles is a respiratory virus, and it transmits from person to person through respiratory droplets, but also in little particles that get suspended in the air,” said Dr. Amesh Adalja, a Pittsburgh-based Infectious Disease Physician. “A person can be in a room and have measles and then leave that room; an hour later, somebody else go into that room and become infected."
So far in 2026, the Pennsylvania Department of Health reported 1,004 cases of measles and five measles-related deaths statewide. Adalja called the outbreak unprecedented.
“The reason why this outbreak has so much momentum is simple – it's because there are not enough people that are vaccinated. And it is finding unvaccinated individuals in many different communities around the state,” Adalja said. “This is the most contagious infectious disease that we know of.”
County health officials said unvaccinated people who believe they were exposed should contact their healthcare provider. They added that it is important to call ahead before visiting a healthcare facility after a potential exposure.

articles.title_orig: Dow Jones Futures: S&P 500 Hits High As Astera, GE Vernova, Arista Lead Buys, But These Stocks Tumble
articles.title_zh: Dow Jones Futures: S&P 500 Hits High As Astera, GE Vernova, Arista Lead Buys, But These Stocks Tumble
articles.content_orig:
The United States stock market has hit an all-time high as excitement around artificial intelligence continues to fuel a buying frenzy on Wall Street.
The S&P 500, the benchmark stock index, closed 0.58 percent higher on Tuesday, topping the previous peak reached in mid-August.
The Nasdaq Composite, which is more heavily weighted towards tech stocks, also hit a record high, finishing up 0.45 percent.
Tech stocks were among the top performers, with each of the “Magnificent Seven” apart from Meta closing higher.
Amazon led the pack with a 1.95 percent gain, followed by Microsoft and Tesla, which rose 0.78 percent and 0.51 percent, respectively.
Apple and Alphabet both rose 0.22 percent, while Nvidia gained 0.14 percent.
Meta, which has risen more than 20 percent since the launch last month of its new AI assistant, Muse, fell 0.41 percent.
Other big movers in tech included Marvell Technology, which rose 5.81 percent, and Cisco, which gained 4.54 percent.
Keith Lerner, chief investment officer and chief market strategist at Truist Advisory Services in Atlanta, Georgia, said the market rally should be seen as a “technology and AI surge”.
“Every bull market has a dominant theme, and technology and AI remain this market’s dominant theme,” Lerner told Al Jazeera.
“Technology and communication services were the only two S&P 500 sectors to rise last month, while the other nine declined.”
Wall Street has shrugged off a host of challenges facing the US economy amid hyperscalers’ multibillion-dollar investments in AI.
Despite the energy crunch caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran and a sell-off of US government bonds partly driven by ballooning government debt, the market is well on track to record its fourth consecutive year of double-digit returns.
The S&P 500 has risen 14 percent so far in 2026, while the Nasdaq Composite is up 18.78 percent.
“Investors remain bullish on the prospects for AI,” Lochlan Halloway, a senior equity strategist at Morningstar Australia, told Al Jazeera.
“They are betting that the money pouring into data centres will earn a good return, and so far that belief has outweighed rising interest rates, more expensive oil and a 10-year bond yield above 5 percent,” Halloway said.
“We are positive on AI too,” Halloway added. “But the range of outcomes is wide, and the market is concentrated in a handful of companies, so the outlook for US shares, and by extension global shares, relies on the AI story continuing to deliver.”
Lerner at Truist Advisory said the market rally had the potential to continue through the end of 2026 given historical trends and expectations for strong corporate earnings.
“We do not expect a straight line higher for markets,” Lerner said.
“Still, the fourth quarter of midterm-election years has produced an average gain of 7 percent and has been positive 84 percent of the time since 1950.”
Lerner said that rising interest rates posed the biggest risk to the upward trend.
“Still, on balance, the weight of the evidence suggests this bull market still has more upside potential,” he said.
Asian stock markets fell on Wednesday, with key indexes in Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong slumping in morning trading.
The Nikkei 225 in Tokyo, Kospi in Seoul and Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong were down 0.79 percent, 1.36 percent and 0.71 percent, respectively, as of 02:30 GMT.
Oil prices, which have been elevated since the start of the war on Iran, rose on Wednesday as traders weighed the fallout of fighting between forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Iran-aligned Houthis.
Brent crude futures for December delivery stood at $101.45 a barrel as of 02:30 GMT, up 0.87 percent.

articles.title_orig: Tropical threat brewing in Gulf could impact U.S. as a hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.title_zh: Tropical threat brewing in Gulf could impact U.S. as a hurricane this weekend. See maps, possible path.
articles.content_orig:
With less than two months remaining in the 2026 hurricane season , the potential for a ninth named tropical storm in the Atlantic basin is brewing in the southern Gulf.
Since the Atlantic's season began on June 1, it has only seen eight named storms this year, while El Niño continues to bring a more active season in the Pacific. The season ends Nov. 30.
Tropical Depression Nine formed in the Gulf on Tuesday. As the storm brews over the warmer waters off Mexico, it's expected to become a tropical storm by early Wednesday and a hurricane on Thursday, according to the National Hurricane Center.
If it does become a tropical storm, it would receive the name Isaias, pronounced "ees-ah-EE-ahs."
Forecast models are beginning to come to agreement that the northward motion of this tropical system brings it to the Gulf Coast this weekend.
Regardless of its name or if it develops into a tropical storm, we do know that it will bring moderate to heavy rainfall to the Gulf Coast and into the rest of the Southeast this weekend into early next week. The hurricane center forecasts 3 to 6 inches of rain for the central Gulf Coast from southeastern Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle.
Some longer-range forecast models also see this moisture eventually reaching the Ohio Valley and Northeast by midweek next week.
Timing, storm intensity and severity of impacts to land with this tropical system are what remain unknown.
While some models have impacts starting Friday evening, others show it beginning later in the weekend.
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis on Tuesday signed an executive order declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of the storm's arrival. DeSantis said in a statement that the order "ensures communities have the time and resources necessary to prepare for potential severe weather impacts to the Panhandle and Big Bend region of Florida."
While tropical storm and hurricane formation and frequency vary throughout the season, the "I"-named systems tend to be the most retired names within the Atlantic basin.
The most commonly known retired "I"-named storms are Ian (2022), Ida (2021), Irma (2017), and Irene (2011).
When Ike was retired in 2008, Isaias replaced the "I" name on the Atlantic tropical cyclones list, which rotates every six years.

articles.title_orig: Are Chinese foreign agent busts on the rise? Federal officials make another arrest
articles.title_zh: Are Chinese foreign agent busts on the rise? Federal officials make another arrest
articles.content_orig:
by GEOFF HARRIS | The National News Desk
WASHINGTON (TNND)  — A woman accused of acting as an agent of China appeared in federal court in Los Angeles this week after prosecutors said she conducted surveillance last year near Seattle targeting the son of Taiwan’s president.
First Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California Bill Essayli said Wanying Zhang was arrested at Los Angeles International Airport.
According to an affidavit, Zhang acted at the direction and control of People’s Republic of China officials to conduct surveillance on family members of a high-ranking Taiwanese government official at their residence in the United States.
The case is the latest in a string of similar arrests pursued by federal officials. Research shows that under the current administration, there have been 60 PRC-related counterintelligence arrests, an 88% increase compared to prior periods.
Among other recent cases, Greg Lui, who was arrested earlier this month for allegedly orchestrating a $300 million illegal AI hardware smuggling ring to China. Plus, Eileen Wang, the former Arcadia, California, mayor, who pleaded guilty this past summer to a federal charge of acting as an unregistered foreign agent for the People’s Republic of China.
After Zhang’s arrest, FBI Director Kash Patel also posted a warning on social media. Writing, “Foreign adversaries take note: America is not your playground.”
When asked whether the number of such cases is likely to rise, Essayli said, “It probably will. And that’s a testament to this administration, the Trump administration and the attorney general, you know, prioritizing the resources of the department.”

articles.content_orig:
Coverage for this event has ended.
President Donald Trump told Fox News correspondent Lucas Tomlinson on Monday that he thinks Iran was behind the attempted attack aboard a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight on Sept. 30.
“And on flydubai. Do you think Iran was responsible for that terrorist attack?” Tomlinson asked.
President Trump said, “I do, I personally do.”
The Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight had landed safely in Saudi Arabia after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who attacked the captain and tried to crash the plane.
The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) said Monday that one of its staff members who had been detained by the Houthis in Yemen was released and reunited with his family.
“We stand in solidarity with the 72 U.N. personnel and five former U.N. personnel, including WFP colleagues, who remain detained in Yemen, and will continue to pursue every possible avenue to secure their immediate and safe release,” the program said in a statement.
WFP joined the U.N. secretary-general in calling for the release of all detained U.N. personnel and other humanitarian workers in Yemen, it added.
U.S. Central Command ( CENTCOM ) said Monday that its forces have redirected 130 ships since the start of its blockade of Iranian ports.
It also confirmed that it had destroyed 13 ships that were violating the blockade or were part of IRGC's multibillion-dollar shadow network.
“The U.S. military remains intensely focused on this mission,” CENTCOM Commander Adm. Brad Cooper said in a post on X .
“We will swiftly act against any vessels trying to run the blockade. Our forces are highly trained, professional, and lethal,” he added.
Norway’s Christian Democratic Party has proposed to establish its own terror blacklist, which would include Hamas, Hezbollah, Palestinian Islamic Jihad and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, The Jerusalem Post .
Norway does not have its own terrorist organization list, instead relying on the UN sanctions framework.
Parliament will vote on whether to instruct the government to develop a system for creating the list, the outlet said. If approved, the government would determine its legal and administrative framework.
“We have been working on this for some time,” Christian Democratic Party lawmaker Joel Ystebø told The Jerusalem Post.
“The reason why we are putting forward this proposal is that many of our allies have their own lists, and we think that would be very good for Norway, too, because it is important to take a stand when it comes to terrorism and antisemitism.."
Saudi-backed Yemeni forces shared a video Monday showing their forces targeting Houthi militia amid reports that the port of Mocha had been recaptured.
“Targeting by our armed forces of elements of the Houthi terrorist militia and its military equipment within Operation ‘Dawn of Yemen,’” the spokesman for the Yemeni Armed Forces said on X .
This came as the Defense Ministry said its armed forces had recaptured Mocha, which the Houthis seized last month.
Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki also said Monday that 100 fighter jets were involved in Operation “Dawn of Yemen,” with forces destroying 324 high-value Houthi targets.
Washington moved 12 American bombers from RAF Fairford in the U.K. on Sunday amid concerns about a potentially complex drone attack ordered by the IRGC, The Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
Citing officials, the outlet reported the planned attack was part of a plot to target the aircraft and kill personnel at the base, including American pilots.
“We do feel with some confidence that the Iranians are trying to do what the Iranian state has done for 49 years, which is engage in acts of terrorism against the United States and against a lot of other people as well,” Vice President JD Vance said Monday. “We are being extremely cautious.”
When pressed by reporters on the tarmac before departing for Grand Island, Nebraska, about whether Iran had brought combat drones into the United Kingdom, President Donald Trump replied, “I can't tell you that,” before stating, “But if they did, they'll suffer greatly.”
The U.K. arrested and released on bail six men over the suspected terror plot as the investigation continues.
The United States, Paraguay, and eight other Western nations issued a joint statement Monday condemning Iranian terrorist activity across the region.
The declaration , which followed a co-hosted Countering Transnational Terrorism Forum between the U.S. and Paraguay, called on Tehran and its proxies to immediately halt all hostile operations.
The nations highlighted ongoing threats including lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, foreign political interference, and efforts to strengthen regional terrorist networks.
The coalition includes Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago, and the U.S.
“This is part of the Trump Administration’s ongoing efforts to reinforce our joint resolve to safeguard our hemisphere’s safety and security,” the State Department said.
The U.S. Treasury Department issued a warning Monday to foreign financial institutions, stating that any continued business with Iran or its financial sector could trigger immediate sanctions without prior notice.
“Foreign financial institutions continuing to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification and should take immediate action to terminate such activity and relationships,” the Treasury Department said.
The Saudi-led coalition said Monday that its forces carried out a military operation in Hodeida province as well as launching a major offensive against the Houthis in the region, Reuters reported.
According to Col. Turki Al-Maliki, the official spokesman for coalition forces, the operation was “to protect maritime navigation security in the Bab al-Mandab Strait.”
“We destroyed weapons depots, boat explosive storage facilities, and naval mines,” Al-Maliki said on X .
“We have thwarted a plot for imminent attacks targeting the waterways south of the Red Sea,” he said, adding that the operation included the “destruction of legitimate military targets belonging to the terrorist Houthi militia.”
"The naval forces of the Coalition carried out a military operation in Al Hudaydah Governorate," Al-Maliki added.
Explosions were heard across the Saudi capital, Riyadh, on Monday, Agence France-Presse (AFP) reported on X.
Reuters also reported that Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said they carried out three military operations targeting several locations in Saudi Arabia , including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, an Aramco refinery in Rabigh, Abha International Airport and the Khamis Mushait military base.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia, the outlet reported.
U.S. sanctions successfully froze Iranian oil exports completely last month as the country's currency plunged to record lows, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Monday.
“Operation Economic Outcast is delivering results: the rial has plunged to record lows, Iran loaded zero crude oil onto tankers last month, and even Iran’s top security official has admitted the country is facing one of the most difficult periods in its history,” Bessent said on X .
“The Iranian regime allows its own people to suffer while it pours resources into terrorism,” he added before vowing that Operation Economic Outcast would not stop until the Iranian regime understands that Washington “will never allow the regime to fund terrorism and develop a nuclear weapon.”
